name: Hezir
overview: Hezir was a male Levite who served as the seventeenth priest chosen among the twenty-four priestly courses established for service in the temple. He belonged to the line of Eleazar, one of the prominent priestly families within the tribe of Levi. His role as a priest highlights his importance in the organized worship and religious duties of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Hezir means 'boar' in Hebrew. This proper name, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:15, does not indicate that it was given directly by God. The meaning itself is straightforward and does not carry additional theological significance within the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Hezir is identified as a descendant of Eleazar, linking him to a significant priestly lineage within the tribe of Levi. Beyond this connection, Scripture does not record other family relationships for Hezir.
scriptureSignificance: Hezir's significance lies in his appointment as the seventeenth priestly leader among the twenty-four courses established by King David for temple service, reflecting the orderly and divinely sanctioned structure of Israel's worship. His placement in the line of Eleazar underscores the continuity of priestly duties passed through faithful descendants. This organization of priestly courses was crucial for maintaining the regular worship of God, highlighting Hezir's role in the spiritual life of Israel.
